picks.headline: AI model predicts pancreatic cancer risk 3 years before diagnosis
picks.excerpt: Mayo Clinic researchers trained an AI model on longitudinal EHR and routine lab data (6,066 patients, 33,396 controls); it reached AUROC 0.853, and a >50% predicted risk meant an 88% chance of diagnosis within a year (ACS Clinical Congress 2026).
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool; Mayo Clinic result on a notoriously late-caught cancer, with hard numbers from routine lab data.

picks.headline: Tumor digital twins: from months to minutes with AI
picks.excerpt: Barcelona Supercomputing Center built MCP servers linking AI agents to NeKo, MaBoSS and PhysiCell so researchers can build tumor digital twins by natural-language conversation, producing model drafts in under 10 minutes instead of months (npj Systems Biology and Applications).
picks.rationale: Most actionable: MCP servers wiring AI agents into real simulation tools, a workflow pattern readers can reuse outside biology.

picks.excerpt: UW-Madison designed quantum nanostructures with vacancy color centers that give optical neural networks strong nonlinearity at power seven orders of magnitude below conventional optical materials (Nature Communications).
picks.title: Tiny quantum nanostructures could make AI less of an energy hog

picks.headline: Stanford Engineers Teach Spacecraft to 'Dream' Their Way to the Space Station
picks.excerpt: A Stanford arXiv preprint builds an AI that runs 'mental simulations' (a learned world model) to plan spacecraft rendezvous and docking, instead of relying only on hard-coded orbital equations and human pilots.
picks.rationale: Adds space/robotics to the mix; world-model planning is a hot AI method shown here in a concrete, high-stakes domain.

picks.headline: When AI disagrees, people change how they perceive the technology, not their original view
picks.excerpt: A University of Michigan study of 482 adults found chatbot agreement boosted confidence, but disagreement did not change minds; instead users judged the AI as machine-like and less likely to consult it again (Computers in Human Behavior Reports).
picks.rationale: Psychology angle with direct product implications: pushback from an AI costs user trust rather than changing minds, so the way an assistant disagrees needs design attention.
